claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection under rapid heating and cooling are governed by the interplay between precursor homogeneity and atomic diffusion during an intermediate thermal dwell.
Optimized precursor blending minimizes initial local concentration gradients.
A precisely timed thermal dwell enables selective diffusion that homogenizes residual inhomogeneities without triggering phase separation.
Refined co-precipitation or solution-based blending can produce an atomically homogeneous Pt–Pd–Au–Ag–Ir precursor.
The relevant processing window is a dwell at 800–900 °C for 30–120 seconds followed by rapid cooling.
Optimized solvent evaporation and reduction protocols ensure precursor homogeneity.
The structural mediator is atomic diffusion at incipient grain boundaries coupled with the absence of initial elemental clusters.
A well-mixed precursor reduces the diffusion distances required during thermal processing.
An intermediate dwell smooths residual concentration gradients and mitigates elemental segregation.
If the dwell is too short, local compositional heterogeneities persist because atomic mobility is insufficient.
If the dwell is too long, over-diffusion may cause phase separation or particle coarsening.
The proposed processing conditions will produce nanoparticles with a uniform lattice parameter relative to the baseline.
The proposed processing conditions will produce a narrower particle-size distribution relative to the baseline.
The proposed processing conditions will minimize elemental segregation and yield a well-defined single-phase solid solution.
Conventional rapid heating and cooling without optimized blending or a dwell typically produces phase separation, elemental segregation, and irregular morphology.
The beneficial effect is confined to 30–120 seconds at 800–900 °C and requires consistently atomic-scale precursor homogeneity.
Departures from the proposed dwell or mixing window can cause coarsening, over-diffusion, or failure to remove concentration gradients.
The optimal dwell time and required mixing quality may vary with synthesis scale and setup.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in phase homogeneity, segregation, and morphology, or failure to identify an optimum within 30–120 seconds, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already described as atomically homogeneous, yet the intervention and conditions propose further enhancement of precursor blending to achieve or ensure that same state, leaving the actual before-versus-after mixing contrast unclear.
